I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $2011 and a pink monopoly with hotels. The opponent has $41 and is in jail. I can trade, unmortgage, or sell buildings.

The opponent has no get-out-of-jail-free card. They have been in jail for two turns and will need to pay $50 or use a card next turn.

The opponent only has $41, so they cannot pay the $50 bail. They will need to sell buildings to exit jail. This is my turn's post-action phase.

I am on NEW_YORK_AVENUE. I had been visiting jail in turn 232. The post-turn phase has no dice roll.

I rolled a 9 to land on New York Avenue. It is mortgaged, so no rent is due.

I will keep both get-out-of-jail-free cards. I will not sell hotels or unmortgage the railroad and Tennessee Avenue. I will avoid trading Tennessee Avenue because that would complete the opponent's orange set. The pink hotels are expensive to maintain.

I am checking standard hotel sellback rules. Boardwalk hotel rent is $2000, leaving me with only $11. Park Place hotel rent is $1500, which I can afford.

Light blue hotels are only $550 to $600 each, so I can afford those. From New York Avenue, rolling a 2 lands on Kentucky or Indiana, both mortgaged and rent-free.

All spaces reachable from New York Avenue are mortgaged or Go to Jail. I cannot land on Park Place or Boardwalk this turn. Rolling a 10 would send me to jail, but I have two get-out-of-jail-free cards.

Jail would protect me from rent while the opponent is trapped. Selling all three brown houses would raise $75, but that still falls short of the $50 bail.

The opponent can exit jail by selling only their brown houses. They would keep both dark blue and light blue hotels.

If they roll a 2 from jail, they land on St. Charles Place and pay $750 in rent. A roll of 4 lands on States Avenue for $750. A roll of 5 lands on Virginia Avenue for $900.

Pennsylvania Railroad is mortgaged and rent-free. The Electric Company and St. James Place are also mortgaged.

The opponent has an 8/36 chance of landing on one of my pink hotels after exiting jail. Only a 2+2 doubles roll would let them leave for free and still hit States Avenue.

Doubles of 3, 4, 5, and 6 would let the opponent exit jail for free without hitting my pink hotels. Only doubles of 1 and 2 remain dangerous.

The opponent has $41, so they cannot pay the $750 or $900 rent on those spaces. They must liquidate assets to survive.

I am estimating liquidation values under standard sellback rules. A brown house sells for $25. A light blue hotel also sells for $25, but returning four houses may complicate the math.

The engine allows selling hotels for substantial cash while keeping dark blue hotels. The opponent can strip light blues and browns for roughly $1011 to pay one pink hotel and still keep their dark blue hotels. A $750 hit would force them to damage a dark-blue hotel too. Dark blue houses and hotels both cost $200.

A dark-blue hotel sells for half its total investment. Each hotel cost $1000 to build, so selling both would raise roughly $1000. That is enough to pay one pink hotel and still keep the other.

A full liquidation would raise about $1491. To pay $750 in rent, the opponent would sell light blue hotels and brown houses for $450, then damage one dark blue hotel by selling three of its houses for $300. Paying $900 in rent would require roughly $859 from buildings alone.

Even a $900 rent hit would leave the opponent with $91 after liquidating one dark blue hotel and their light blue and brown holdings. A $750 hit leaves them with $41. Neither pink hotel can bankrupt them because they have accumulated enough liquidation value from those properties.

I am weighing whether to unmortgage the Pennsylvania Railroad. It would cost $220 and yield only $25 in rent, so it offers little value.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue is also pointless. The other orange properties are mortgaged, so no orange monopoly exists, and the $14 rent would be negligible. I will not sell my pink hotels either; the engine's exact sellback value for a hotel stack is unclear.

Selling the pink hotels would destroy my only rent drain and raise only about fifty dollars, so I will not do it. I am now considering trading my get-out-of-jail-free cards to help the opponent exit jail, though they will be forced out on their next roll anyway.

I will not trade my get-out-of-jail-free card. That would let the opponent avoid paying $50 bail and still land on my pink hotels. I need that card for when I am sent to jail, since jail would protect me from their dark blue rent while they walk into my pink properties. I am now considering whether to buy their dark blue hotels to break their monopoly.

I cannot buy one of their dark blue hotels to break the monopoly. The engine prevents trading a property that still has buildings on it, and a hotel means the opponent owns the entire set. They would have to sell all buildings first before I could trade for one space.

I am now considering a massive trade offer to acquire Boardwalk. The opponent would need to sell their dark blue hotels first, which they will not do unless the price is enormous. I could offer all my cash plus Tennessee Avenue and both get-out-of-jail-free cards for Boardwalk, but the opponent has no incentive to accept such a deal.

The opponent would have to sell both their Boardwalk and Park Place hotels to trade Boardwalk for me. That would destroy their only dark blue rent threat entirely.

I cannot trade cash for Boardwalk. That would bankrupt me against the light blue hotels, which cost over five hundred dollars each. I need a large cash cushion to survive those spaces, so I will not give away my money.

I rejected trading Tennessee Avenue for cash. The opponent already turned down a $400 offer when they had more money, and now they cannot pay it anyway. Giving them Tennessee would complete their orange monopoly, which is dangerous even without houses.

Unmortgaging the orange set would cost about three hundred dollars, which the opponent cannot afford. Building houses on those properties is also impossible without liquidating hotels first.

The opponent has no get-out-of-jail-free cards to trade. I will end my turn, since no optional action is beneficial.

I am now considering whether the $11 margin above Boardwalk rent is too thin to be truly safe. I will not attempt any trade that could bankrupt the opponent or force a mistake, since they have already rejected poor offers.

No optional action can raise cash without cost. Passing GO would only move the piece, not generate income. The opponent would land with $2041 after paying Boardwalk rent, while I would have just $11 remaining. I can survive that single hit by selling my pink hotels for a cushion, but another rent would bankrupt me unless I liquidate those hotels again.
